key_driver_codes: Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC
Degenerative Nervous System Disorders without MCC
Vaginal Delivery with O.R. Procedures Except Sterilization and/or D&C
patterns_data.pattern_details: A large share of the observed spend change appears tied to authorization code redistribution and claims falling into unmapped facility buckets, especially in FL and secondarily in NY, TN, and IA. Because these shifts can change where dollars appear without reflecting a true care change, business action on utilization, provider performance, or reimbursement should wait until coding and mapping are reconciled. This is a gating issue for the rest of the analysis.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If these classification shifts are not corrected first, UM, network, and reimbursement actions may target the wrong problem.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile authorization code logic and facility mapping for the affected FL, NY, TN, and IA claims, then rerun the impacted authorization and provider views before taking policy or contract action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The evidence explicitly shows authorization code movement and unmapped facility values that require data validation before operational interpretation.
evidence_summary: FL authorization code redistribution accounts for about +$127.5M and is flagged for validation before action.
NY / TN authorization code redistribution adds about +$5.5M, concentrated in a delivery-related inpatient DRG and two hospitals.
IA LTSS Dual Eligible claims in Not Mapped facilities add about +$11.1M in volume-led change, with another +$4.7M showing mixed volume and unit-cost pressure.
A smaller FL Not Mapped TANF Standard spike adds about +$105K and reinforces the facility classification issue.

patterns_data.pattern_details: FL authorized SNF spend rose sharply across both LTSS Dual Eligible and LTSS Non Dual products, with the increase driven mainly by more admissions and claims rather than pure pricing. Neurologic degeneration and musculoskeletal aftercare are the main clinical contributors, and the related NF aftercare pattern supports a sustained post-acute demand story. This is the clearest operational utilization increase after removing the validation noise.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is a major post-acute cost driver with direct levers in authorization, discharge planning, and SNF network management.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a targeted FL SNF review for LTSS members focused on admission appropriateness, continued-stay decisions, discharge pathways, and free-standing SNF network performance.
evidence_summary: FL LTSS Dual Eligible authorized SNF spend increased about +$136.1M, including roughly +13,000 admissions and +22,577 claims.
FL LTSS Non Dual authorized SNF spend added about +$17.7M with roughly +1,880 admissions and +5,759 claims.
The largest clinical drivers are degenerative nervous system disorders and musculoskeletal aftercare, including about +$13.1M from Degenerative Nervous System Disorders without MCC.
Related FL NF orthopedic aftercare adds about +$1.5M, supporting continued post-acute care intensity rather than a one-time spike.

IN and KS are heavily concentrated in Alzheimer's, stroke sequelae, hemiplegia, and Parkinson's diagnoses, while the operational SNF patterns show materially higher admissions across LTSS products. The combined picture points to durable long-stay care demand and case-mix pressure.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: These members are likely to keep driving post-acute cost unless care management, placement, and length-of-stay levers are applied to the specific neurologic cohorts.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Create a joint clinical and UM worklist in CA, IN, and KS for dementia, stroke sequelae, and Parkinson's members in NF/SNF settings, with emphasis on level-of-care appropriateness and discharge alternatives.
evidence_summary: CA / IN / KS LTSS Dual Eligible free-standing SNF spend increased about +$41.7M and was volume-led.
IN NF case-mix growth totals about +$38.0M when combining the two IN NF groupings, centered in Alzheimer's and post-stroke hemiplegia diagnoses.
KS NF case-mix growth adds about +$12.0M, again concentrated in post-stroke hemiplegia and Parkinson's diagnoses.
CA LTSS Non Dual free-standing SNF adds about +$9.6M, showing that the broader SNF pattern extends beyond one product.

patterns_data.top_pattern: FL acute hospital spend is concentrated in a few authorized provider and product combinations
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: FL Medicaid ACUTE HOSPITAL admissions across ABD Non Dual, TANF Standard, and CHIP Standard
patterns_data.pattern_details: FL acute hospital spend growth is concentrated in a small set of authorized products and hospitals, which creates a clear provider-mix story. ABD Non Dual shows both more admissions and higher paid per admit, with Tampa General standing out on unit cost, while TANF Standard is mainly a volume story across Tampa General, AdventHealth Orlando, and Lakeland. CHIP Standard adds a smaller but similar acute hospital increase at AdventHealth Orlando.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Because the pressure is concentrated, provider-specific contract, pricing, and authorization actions are more likely to work than broad market-wide changes.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run provider-level contract and authorization review for Tampa General, AdventHealth Orlando, and Lakeland across the affected FL acute hospital products, prioritizing Tampa General ABD Non Dual pricing and TANF Standard admission growth.
evidence_summary: FL ABD Non Dual acute hospital spend increased about +$21.1M with roughly +1,169 admissions and higher paid per admit.
Tampa General alone added about +$3.7M in FL ABD Non Dual acute hospital spend, with paid per admit up about $8K.
FL TANF Standard acute hospital spend increased about +$15.4M with roughly +2,263 admissions, while paid per admit declined, confirming a volume-led provider mix shift.
A smaller FL acute hospital increase remains in ABD Non Dual and CHIP Standard at AdventHealth Orlando and Lakeland, adding about +$940K combined.

patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review maternity episodes by hospital and state for delivery coding, complication mix, maternal-neonatal linkage, and admission management, starting with Indiana acuity drivers and Tennessee volume growth.

NY Family Care, OH TANF Standard, and KS TANF Standard together add about +$1.6M around the same delivery DRG.
The shared delivery DRG across operational and clinical views suggests a repeatable maternity episode pattern rather than a single hospital anomaly.

patterns_data.top_pattern: FL has rare catastrophic inpatient outliers that need case-level review
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: FL rare high-cost IP Med/Surg and IP NICU admissions
key_driver_codes: Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell and Other Immunotherapies
ECMO or Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck with Major O.R. Procedures
Extreme Immaturity or Respiratory Distress Syndrome, Neonate
patterns_data.pattern_details: A very small number of FL inpatient cases are driving disproportionate spend, including CAR-T therapy, ECMO or tracheostomy-level care, and NICU extreme immaturity or respiratory distress admissions. These are not broad utilization trends; they are catastrophic or highly specialized cases with very high cost per admission. The right response is case-level validation and high-cost case management, not broad policy edits.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Rare catastrophic claims can materially distort trend and require immediate clinical, claims, and stop-loss style review.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Audit the individual FL outlier admissions for DRG and diagnosis alignment, confirm pricing and authorization handling, and route validated cases to catastrophic case management and reinsurance review.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is driven by very small numbers of highly unusual, very high-cost admissions, including clinically atypical coding combinations that should be confirmed case by case.
evidence_summary: One CAR-T leukemia admission at Tampa General added about +$771K.
Two ECMO or tracheostomy-level admissions at AdventHealth Orlando added about +$857K, or about $428K per admission.
A separate FL NICU pattern at AdventHealth Orlando added about +$981K across 12 admissions, with paid per admit up about $29K.
All drivers are low-volume and high-severity, so case-level review is more appropriate than broad utilization action.

patterns_data.pattern_details: NC shows a small-number but high-cost behavioral health spike centered in foster care acute psych and related inpatient behavioral health diagnoses. Paid per admit increased sharply, and the clinical pattern is concentrated in PTSD, adjustment disorder, and stress-reaction diagnoses rather than broad psychiatric utilization. This looks like a focused vulnerable-member cohort that needs targeted intervention.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Even low-volume behavioral health spikes can indicate network, placement, or case management gaps in a high-risk population.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review NC foster care behavioral health episodes for setting appropriateness, length of stay, specialty facility pricing, and recurring-member case management, with escalation for any out-of-network or prolonged stays.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The spend is concentrated in low-volume, high-cost admissions and should be confirmed at the case level before broader policy conclusions are drawn.
evidence_summary: NC acute psych TANF Foster Care spend increased about +$1.9M across 46 admissions, with paid per admit up about $41K.
The NC IP BH clinical pattern adds about +$1.8M across PTSD, adjustment disorder, stress reaction, and OCD-related admissions.
Clinical paid per admit ranges from about $33K to $100K in the top cases.
The pattern is small in count but concentrated enough to warrant immediate case-management and pricing review.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Authorized acute hospital and SNF episodes in NY, TN, and IN with concentrated provider-level pressure
key_driver_codes: Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Outside the major markets, a small set of authorized episodes in NY, TN, and IN shows concentrated provider-level cost pressure. NY LTSS Dual SNF looks like a reimbursement issue because paid per admit increased while allowed per admit fell, while NY TANF Standard and IN Family Care include very small-count acute hospital spikes and TN ABD Non Dual reflects localized hospital admission growth. These are targeted exceptions rather than broad market trends.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Narrow provider or claim-level issues can often be corrected faster through contract, pricing, or claim review than through broad operational programs.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run provider- and claim-level review for the named NY, TN, and IN episodes to confirm contract application, pricing accuracy, and authorization-to-payment consistency before expanding action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Several drivers are single-case or very low-volume spikes, so claim-level confirmation is appropriate before escalation to network or policy changes.
evidence_summary: NY LTSS Dual Eligible free-standing SNF adds about +$2.0M with roughly +241 admissions and paid per admit up while allowed per admit declined.
TN ABD Non Dual acute hospital adds about +$559K at Ascension Saint Thomas Rutherford Hospital with roughly +63 admissions.
IN Family Care acute hospital includes one admission adding about +$435K.
NY TANF Standard acute hospital adds about +$464K across two admissions, or about $114K per admission.
